In detail

El Carmel has the strongest documented safety concerns in the district. Around the Bunkers del Carmel viewpoint, residents describe their street as 'the worst street in Barcelona,' citing a violent robbery by minors, an assault on a neighbour who confronted late-night revellers, vandalism, and squatters throwing large parties — prompting the city to install €1.4M anti-crowding fencing to close the viewpoint at 10pm. More recently: a mass brawl with a stabbing and 13 arrests at El Coll-La Teixonera metro station (5 Apr 2026), a suspect linked to ~16 break-ins arrested, and a kidnapping/attempted-murder arrest. Daytime risk is mainly pickpocketing/burglary; night-time, especially around the bunkers viewpoint and metro area, carries real risk of confrontational violence. Sources checked: Metròpoli Obert, 12 Nov 2022; elindependiente.com, 9 Apr 2023; barnadiario.com, Dec 2024-Apr 2026.

This rating comes from a structured local-source assessment. This specific area was reviewed against credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — and the signals were consolidated across sources rather than taken from any single report, with the reasoning and the sources shown above. Barcelona publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does publish one, Wandroz uses it instead of an assessment. Where a review finds nothing documented, that is recorded as no findings rather than as a safety rating.

Frequently asked questions

Is el Carmel safe?

Wandroz currently rates el Carmel in Barcelona as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Barcelona during the day and an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Barcelona at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Barcelona publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is el Carmel safe at night?

At night, el Carmel is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Barcelona. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is el Carmel a good area to stay in as a tourist?

el Carmel's day rating (roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Barcelona) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. Is there official crime data for el Carmel?

Not an official government crime feed — el Carmel's rating comes from Wandroz's own current local/national press and survey research for this specific area instead (see the note on this page for what was checked and the sources used).
